One of, if not [i]the[/i] weirdest game I've ever played.

Even though this experience is only around 1 and a half hour to play through; it feels lot longer and I mean that the best way possible. There's so much quality stuff here, it's so captivating and overwhelming and the game acts like it's nothing. So many interesting characters with all sorts of styles, animations and voices; so many diverse places with so much personality and ideas, it feels like they could go on forever, but they still manage to feel connected and consistent.

It all feels like a trip, it's so out there, I don't even know where to begin or what to say about it; you just have to see it for yourself, you'll get it the first minute you boot it up.

I'll say this though, it feels one of the bests out of the bunch that are aiming for a similar experience. It does not feel cheap at all; there's so much quality here with it's presentation, it's surreal, humorous, uncanny, existential tone. If I would have payed for this game I still would have been satisfied; but with no price tag it actually feels criminal playing this for free, even if it's not your cup of tea.

So what do you have to lose; it's free, might as well try it!
It's only one chapter so far, it's clear there's more content and chapters planned in the future; but it still feels like a compact experience with some conclusion, but with mysteries and lore still open. I really hope they are still working on it and make it a full game eventually; I'd happily pay for it once it's out. Even though I haven't played LSD: Dream Emulator; that seems like the closest comparison in terms of weirdness and style, but this one feels a bit less cryptic and more straight forward with tasks and objectives. If that one or Jazzpunk, Kid A Mnesia Exhibition, Manifold Garden, Antichamber or any other trippy, weird experiences are up your alley; this seems like an obvious choice!

I used to think that surrealism was just really random. I still liked it, but thought it was randomness. 
ENA and her world is proof that randomness couldn't make a great surrealist world. Everything feels very intentional, like there is meaning in the world you're in, despite it being very very confusing. That gives the world a personality and gives a sense of life that wouldn't be achieved through randomness.
Secondly, the animators were locked in SO hard making these animations. My personal favorite thing about this game is just seeing how creative and fluid each animation can be. 
This is not free slop. The idea that this is free is baffling to me. Please take the time for yourself to experience the world that ENA dream bbq manages to create. It may not make a ton of sense at first (or ever). But you'll find yourself enjoying it for some reason.

The voice actors are wonderfully entertaining to listen to in clips and I wish I could get caught up in the gameplay so I  could experience more of their characters. 

Overall the game is steeped in surrealism and puzzling fetch quests. I hope more people find joy in the full experience of ENA Dream BBQ.
